paragraphs: Argyll and Bute Council's family placement team recruits and supports foster carers for children in care across the council area, and its service is shown above with the independent agencies that cover Argyll and Bute. The council needs emergency carers who take a child overnight or for a couple of days, short-term carers for a few weeks or months, long-term carers who may look after a child for the rest of their childhood, and respite carers who give full-time carers a break.

The council says it particularly needs carers for teenagers and for sibling groups who need a home where they can stay together. Its service aims include keeping brothers and sisters together when it is safe, in line with the Promise, and giving carers trauma-informed preparation, training and supervision.

To foster with the council you need to be over 21, in reasonable health, eligible to join the PVG scheme run by Disclosure Scotland, and have suitable accommodation. You can be of any gender, sexual orientation or relationship status. The first step is a preparation group where you meet experienced carers; if you then apply, the assessment includes medical and police checks and involves everyone in your household.

Argyll and Bute Council publishes its 2026/27 fostering rates as one weekly sum for each child, covering the child's day-to-day costs and including a component for the carer. Its rate table gives £300.51 a week for a child aged 0 to 4, £302.94 for 5 to 10, £360.60 for 11 to 15 and £393.39 for 16 and 17; the breakdown further down the same page adds up to a little more for the 5 to 10 and 16 to 17 bands, so ask the family placement team which figure applies. The carer's component inside those sums is £103.80 a week for children up to 10 and £120.20 from 11. Money for birthdays, religious festivals and holidays is built into the weekly rate rather than paid separately, carers have 14 nights of paid respite a year without any cut to the allowance, mileage over 50 miles for a child can be claimed at 45p a mile, and payments go into the carer's bank account every fortnight. Our Argyll and Bute pay page sets the figures out in full.

Agencies set their own pay and support, so ask each one what it would pay for a child of the age you hope to care for and compare it with the council's figures. Speak to two or three of the services above, including the council's family placement team, before you decide, and see our page for Scotland as a whole if you live near the edge of the council area.
